quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power can the front brake provide?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Provide you with an escape route.
Welcome other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Welcome other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid hazards, escape from danger, and stay out of other vehicles' blind spots. Your position should discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: In New York State, a driver with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of _____ is legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In New York State, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. You cannot operate a vehicle at this level.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes suddenly while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: Straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars before stopping. If you cannot straighten out, apply the brakes smoothly, reduce your lean, then increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: At night, how should your following distance compare to daytime following distance?

options.text: You should allow a longer following distance at night.
You should allow a shorter following distance at night.
You should maintain the same following distance at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances because you lack visual cues like shadows and light contrast. Always use a longer following distance when riding at night.

questions.question: Approved helmets:

options.text: Can limit the view of the rider.
Allow the rider to see as far to the sides as needed.
Do not have to be worn if you think your view will be limited.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the rider to see as far to the sides as needed.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not limit your vision. They allow you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. Slow down and prepare to yield to pedestrians and vehicles. Stop if necessary. Proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does your body eliminate per hour?
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour on average. The time needed varies, so do not drive after any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire provides power, so you lose acceleration.
The shake makes it hard to use mirrors.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects steering. If this happens while riding, safely exit the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: A proper lane position can help you do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.

questions.explanation: Lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and set up for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: In New York State, outside of New York City, you may _______ when you see a solid red traffic light at an intersection.
questions.explanation: In New York State, except in New York City, you can turn right at a red light. First, you must come to a complete stop. Then, you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic. In New York City, you can only turn right on red if a sign says it is allowed.

questions.question: Signs that show where services are located are:

options.text: Blue with white letters or symbols
Green with white letters or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters or symbols
questions.explanation: Service signs show where rest areas, gas stations, campgrounds, and hospitals are located. These signs are blue with white letters and symbols.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
Ride in the center of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: The center of a lane becomes very slippery when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is usually the safest choice.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make it lean, press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for at least one hour
After riding for more than 8 hours

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips. They usually occur within five miles of where the rider starts, just a few minutes after riding begins.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Reduce their usual space cushions by half

questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: Of crashes between motorcycles and cars, how many are caused by car drivers failing to give the right-of-way to the motorcycle?
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because the car driver does not give the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the total stopping power.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other
Do both actions at the same time
Choose to do only one action
Only use the front brake to stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve to avoid a crash, do these actions separately. Do not brake and swerve at the same time because it may cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do both at the same time

questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, do each action separately. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.
